_meta.name: abstract_rare_v1
_meta.purpose: Third eval set. Questions are anchored on high-IDF terms that appear in a paper's ABSTRACT BODY but NOT in its title. This removes the confound present in lexical_entity_v1, where every chunk begins with 'Title: ...' and every question reused title tokens, causing all methods to saturate at 98-100%.
_meta.hypothesis: Sparse retrieval (BM25) and hybrid outperform dense-only here. Rationale: bi-encoder embeddings compress a whole chunk into one vector, smoothing over low-frequency tokens that carry little semantic weight but high discriminative power. Exact term matching does not smooth.
_meta.construction: Terms selected programmatically: tokens with IDF > 6.5 present in the abstract but absent from the title. Questions written around the strongest technical/entity terms only; common English words that happen to be corpus-rare ('wishing', 'arrive') were discarded as unnatural query material.
honest_caveats: Constructed to favour lexical retrieval. Must be reported alongside eval_dataset.json (paraphrase, dense-favouring) and lexical_entity_v1 (saturated). No single set characterises this system.
Some anchor terms are obscure enough that a real user would be unlikely to query them. This is a lexical STRESS TEST, not a model of the production query distribution.
n=30 is small; a single question shifts Recall@3 by 3.3 points. Treat margins under ~7 points as noise.
_meta.id_format: Bare arXiv ID, no prefix, no version suffix.
